text:
Maya: pushed a follow-up RFC draft for on-prem / air-gapped packaging + upgrade strategy. Main proposal: signed bootstrap tarball for initial install, runtime delivered as OCI images for ongoing upgrades (seedable registry), two upgrade modes (atomic full-image swap and optional delta patching), and a controller that verifies signatures and orchestrates staged rollouts. Draft: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/onprem-upgrades (private). Asking for feedback on tradeoffs and edge cases.

Aj: high-level looks good — quick Q: for deltas are we leaning bsdiff/bspatch or OCI image layer deltas? bsdiff is smaller but CPU-heavy, image layer diffs rely on registry/content-addressability.

Liam: in many air-gapped customers CPU and temp disk are constrained. For those, full-image swaps are simpler and more predictable. Image-layer dedupe (content-addressable storage) + compressed layers probably wins operationally.

Jordan: we should support both modes and let operator choose per-cluster. Important: upgrades must be atomic from the service perspective and support fast rollback. Also add a "rollback window" config so controller can auto-rollback on X% errors in Y minutes.

Maya: agreed. proposal: default to "atomic" upgrades; enable "delta" when cluster has a patch-worker label (allows operators to declare machines that can accept CPU-heavy patching). Also: signed manifest format (example below) and signature verification using customer-provided public keys or our CA for Dedicated.

Maya (example manifest):
```
component: runtime
version: 1.2.0
bundle: runtime-1.2.0.tar.gz
sha256: 3a7f9d...
patches:
  - from: 1.1.3
    diff: runtime-1.1.3->1.2.0.bsdiff
    sha256: d1e4f2...
migrations:
  - id: 202402_add_index
    script: migrations/202402_add_index.sql
    when: post-unpack
signatures:
  - keyid: key-prod-1
    sig: MEUCIQ...
```

Aj: two more concerns: key management in air-gapped installs (how do we rotate/expire keys?) and bootstrap trust (how does the first key get provisioned?).

Olivia: from customer/product side: enterprise buyers expect BYO keys (HSM/KMS). We should support a simple workflow: during onboarding operator supplies a public key file or imports into a KMS; for air-gapped, we accept a signed `trust-manifest` that is applied once during install. Need docs + checklist.

Maya: plan: support three trust modes: 1) bring-your-own-public-key (BYOPK) — operator uploads pub key, 2) KMS/HSM integration for Dedicated and Private (we store key refs, never private key), 3) offline trust manifest — a signed bundle containing allowed key fingerprints for bootstrap. We'll include rotation commands and a documented rotation cadence.

Liam: also think about storage: OCI images plus seed registry tarball might be big. Recommend we publish a `registry-seed` tar with only required layers + delta metadata. Provide `registry-init` tool that imports the tar into Harbor/registry. Example: 
```
# on air-gapped host
./registry-init --import registry-seed-1.2.0.tar.gz --registry http://local-reg:5000
./redwood-operator install --bundle bootstrap-1.2.0.tar.gz --verify-key pub.pem
```

Jordan: DB/schema migrations are always risky. Proposal: migration hooks must be idempotent and accompanied by a migration lock. Controller should snapshot metadata (or create a logical backup) before running migrations. If migration fails, operator can auto-rollback the runtime, but DB downgrades must be manual with an explicit approval flow.

Maya: agreed — we'll require migrations to include a `precheck` script that exits non-zero on unsafe conditions and a `dry-run` mode in the operator. Add that to the manifest schema.

Aj: about signatures: prefer COSE or OpenPGP? COSE works well for small embedded tooling, OpenPGP is familiar. We should standardize on one and provide sign/verify tooling. Also include timestamped attestation to avoid replay.

Maya: leaning COSE + ed25519 for compactness; we'll produce CLI helpers: `redwood-sign` and `redwood-verify`. For Dedicated we can add optional integration to customer KMS via gRPC to keep private keys out of our control.

Olivia: for upgrades UX: customers want canary/staged rollouts across nodes. In fully air-gapped sites without controller connectivity to our cloud, controller runs locally and supports staged percent-based rollouts (e.g., 10% -> 50% -> 100%) and health checks. Must be plumbed into manifest: rollout strategy + probe config.

Maya: yep — rollout example in manifest: `rollout: { type: staged, steps: [10, 50, 100], pause: 10m }` (we'll document schema).

Liam: operational notes: make sure operator mode can pause and resume upgrades; also provide a way to force-invalidate local cache if images are corrupted. Add a `reconcile --force` flag to operator.

Jordan: on rollback semantics: if rollback fails due to DB incompatibility, operator surfaces a blocking incident to ops-team with logs and retains previous images/artifacts for forensic analysis.

ops-bot: Created issue #2345: "On-prem upgrade manifest schema + operator hooks" and linked the draft RFC.

Aj: I'll take the key management and signature format follow-up; will draft a short appendix with examples for COSE and OpenPGP.

Maya: thanks. next steps: I'll update the RFC to include manifest schema (with precheck/dry-run/migration-lock/rollout), two-mode upgrade strategy, seed registry workflow, and key/trust modes. Please comment on the doc by EOD Wednesday. :thumbsup:

Olivia: :thumbsup:

Liam: noted, will add resource constraints section for tiny-footprint installs.

Jordan: will write operator-runbook for emergency rollback flows.

Maya: great — closing loop here, will iterate on doc and ping infra for a short design review next week.
